sections.title: 1. Article 1 & 2 - Union of States & Admission/Establishment of New States

masteryZone.q: Which of the following describes the nature of the Indian federation under Article 1?
opts: An indestructible union of indestructible states
A destructible union of destructible states
An indestructible union of destructible states
A destructible union of indestructible states
masteryZone.sol: India is an 'indestructible union of destructible states' because the Union cannot be dissolved, but the borders and existence of states can be changed by Parliament.

masteryZone.q: Which territories are included under the 'Territory of India' in Article 1(3)? (Select all that apply)
opts: Territories of the States
Union Territories
Territories that may be acquired by the Government of India
Adjacent international waters beyond 12 nautical miles
masteryZone.sol: The Territory of India includes the states, the union territories, and any future acquired territories. It does not include international waters.

masteryZone.q: True or False: The term 'Union of India' includes the Union Territories.
masteryZone.sol: False. The 'Union of India' includes only the states, whereas the 'Territory of India' includes both states and Union Territories.

masteryZone.q: Fill in the blank: Article ______ of the Constitution deals with the admission or establishment of new states that are not part of India.
masteryZone.sol: Article 2 deals with the admission or establishment of new external states.

masteryZone.q: Match the term with its correct definition under Article 1:

options.text: Name of the country specified in Article 1
Polity structure reflecting no right of secession
Wider expression including States, UTs, and acquired lands

masteryZone.sol: Name matches India/Bharat; Polity matches Union of States; and Territory is the wider expression.

masteryZone.q: Give one example of an external territory admitted into the Union of India as a state under Article 2.
masteryZone.sol: Sikkim (admitted in 1975).

masteryZone.q:
Assertion (A): Dr. B.R. Ambedkar preferred the phrase 'Union of States' over 'Federation of States'.
Reason (R): The states of India did not enter into an agreement to form the Union, and no state has the right to secede.
Select the correct code:
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
masteryZone.sol: Both statements are true, and the reason explains why the phrase was preferred.

masteryZone.q:
Consider the following statements regarding acquired territories:
Statement I: The Government of India can acquire foreign territories under international law.
Statement II: Acquired territories are automatically counted under the 'Territory of India' immediately upon acquisition.
Which of the following is correct?
opts: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement II is correct but Statement I is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
masteryZone.sol: Both statements are correct. India can acquire foreign lands, and these are categorized under Article 1(3)(c).

masteryZone.q: Why is the term 'Territory of India' considered constitutionally wider than the 'Union of India'?
masteryZone.sol: Because the 'Territory of India' encompasses states, union territories, and any future acquired lands, while the 'Union of India' refers only to the states that form the federal system.

masteryZone.q: How was Sikkim integrated into the Union of India under Article 2?
masteryZone.sol: Sikkim was first made an 'Associate State' through the 35th Constitutional Amendment (1974), and later, following a referendum, it was admitted as a full 22nd state of the Union through the 36th Constitutional Amendment (1975).

masteryZone.q: The government of India purchases an island from a neighboring country in 2027. Under which Article of the Constitution can this island be administered as a new territory?
masteryZone.sol: It would be administered as an acquired territory under Article 1(3)(c). To officially admit or establish it as a State of the Union, Parliament would exercise its powers under Article 2.

masteryZone.q: Explain the constitutional significance of Article 1 and Article 2 of the Indian Constitution.
masteryZone.sol: Article 1 defines the name of the country (India/Bharat) and establishes its indestructible federal nature as a 'Union of States'. It also outlines the territorial classification. Article 2 grants Parliament the exclusive power to admit or establish new states from territories that are not currently part of the Union, dealing with external adjustments.

sections.title: 2. Article 3 - Alteration of Areas, Boundaries or Names of Existing States

masteryZone.q: A bill to alter the boundary of an existing state can be introduced in Parliament only on the recommendation of:
opts: The Governor of the concerned state
The President of India
The Prime Minister of India
The Chief Minister of the concerned state
masteryZone.sol: Prior recommendation of the President is mandatory for introducing any bill under Article 3.

masteryZone.q: Which of the following actions can Parliament take regarding states under Article 3? (Select all that apply)
opts: Increase the area of any state
Diminish the area of any state
Alter the name of any state
Force a state to merge with a neighboring country
masteryZone.sol: Parliament can increase, diminish, or rename states. It has no power under Article 3 to secede or merge a state with a foreign country.

masteryZone.q: True or False: If a state legislature does not send its views within the specified time, the reorganization bill cannot be introduced.
masteryZone.sol: False. Parliament can proceed even if the state legislature fails to express its views within the prescribed time limit.

masteryZone.q: Fill in the blank: Parliament can reorganize existing states under Article 3 by passing the bill with a ______ majority.
masteryZone.sol: The correct answer is simple majority.

masteryZone.q: Match the steps of Article 3 procedure with their correct sequence:

items.left: I. President refers bill to State Legislature
II. Bill introduced with President's recommendation
III. Parliament votes by Simple Majority

options.text: Step taken to consult the affected state's views
Final voting requirement in both houses

masteryZone.sol: Recommendation is the initial step; referral to the state is the consultative step; simple majority vote is the final legislative step.

masteryZone.q: Are the views of the state legislature regarding a boundary change binding on the President or Parliament?
masteryZone.sol: No, they are strictly advisory and not binding.

masteryZone.q:
Assertion (A): Parliament can alter the borders of any state without the consent of that state.
Reason (R): The Indian Constitution does not guarantee the territorial integrity of any state.
Select the correct code:
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
masteryZone.sol: Both statements are true. Parliament has unilateral power because states do not have guaranteed territorial boundaries, illustrating why India is a union of destructible states.

masteryZone.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Article 3 bills:
Statement I: If a bill is amended in Parliament, it must be referred back to the state legislature for fresh views.
Statement II: The bill can be introduced in either the Lok Sabha or the Rajya Sabha.
Which of the following is correct?
opts: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement II is correct but Statement I is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
masteryZone.sol: Statement I is incorrect because no fresh reference is required for subsequent amendments. Statement II is correct: the bill can be introduced in either house.

masteryZone.q: Why does Article 3 require referring the bill to the concerned State Legislature if their views are not binding on Parliament?
masteryZone.sol: To respect the federal spirit and give the affected state an opportunity to express its local concerns, though the ultimate sovereign power rests with the Union Parliament.

masteryZone.q: How can the name of an existing state of India be altered?
masteryZone.sol: By introducing a bill in either House of Parliament with the prior recommendation of the President, referring it to the state legislature for advisory views, and passing it with a simple majority in both houses of Parliament.

masteryZone.q: The Parliament of India introduces a bill to split state X into two states. State X's assembly passes a unanimous resolution opposing the split. Examine the legal validity of the split if Parliament passes the bill.
masteryZone.sol: The split is completely valid. Under Article 3, the consent or opposition of the state legislature is not binding. Parliament has the absolute constitutional authority to reorganize, split, or merge states regardless of their assemblies' opposition.

masteryZone.q: Explain the step-by-step process of state reorganization under Article 3 of the Indian Constitution.
masteryZone.sol: First, a bill is drafted. It requires the prior recommendation of the President before introduction. Second, the President refers the bill to the affected state legislature for views within a specified time. Third, once the views are received (or the time expires), the bill is introduced in either house of Parliament. Finally, it must be passed by a simple majority of members present and voting in both houses to be sent for the President's assent.

masteryZone.q: Under Article 4, laws passed for state reorganization are not considered constitutional amendments under:
opts: Article 356
Article 360
Article 368
Article 370
masteryZone.sol: Article 4 declares that laws made under Articles 2 and 3 are not to be deemed as amendments of the Constitution under Article 368.

masteryZone.q: Which of the following commissions/committees recommended that language should NOT be the primary basis for state reorganization? (Select all that apply)
opts: Dhar Commission
JVP Committee
Fazl Ali Commission
Sarkaria Commission
masteryZone.sol: The Dhar Commission (1948) and the JVP Committee (1948) rejected language as the basis. The Fazl Ali Commission (1953) accepted language as a major factor.

masteryZone.q: True or False: Ceding Indian territory to a foreign nation can be done through a normal law passed by a simple majority under Article 3.
masteryZone.sol: False. Ceding territory requires a constitutional amendment under Article 368, as ruled in the Berubari Union case.

masteryZone.q: Fill in the blank: The States Reorganisation Act of 1956 created 14 states and ______ union territories.
masteryZone.sol: The Act created 14 states and 6 union territories.

masteryZone.q: Match the states with their year of formation/reorganization:
masteryZone.sol: Andhra was formed in 1953, Gujarat in 1960, and Telangana in 2014.

masteryZone.q: Which constitutional amendment abolished the classification of states into Part A, B, C, and D?
masteryZone.sol: Seventh Constitutional Amendment Act, 1956.

masteryZone.q:
Assertion (A): Ceding Indian territory to Bangladesh in 2015 required the 100th Constitutional Amendment Act.
Reason (R): Any boundary settlement with a foreign power requires an amendment under Article 368.
Select the correct code:
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
masteryZone.sol: The assertion is true (100th amendment swapped enclaves). The reason is false because simple boundary settlement disputes do not require a constitutional amendment; only actual cession of territory does.

masteryZone.q:
Consider the following statements regarding post-independence integration:
Statement I: Junagadh joined India via plebiscite.
Statement II: Hyderabad joined India via police action.
Which of the following is correct?
opts: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement II is correct but Statement I is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
masteryZone.sol: Both statements represent correct historical integration methods for these princely states.

masteryZone.q: Why did the creation of Andhra State in 1953 force the government to appoint the Fazl Ali Commission?
masteryZone.sol: The creation of Andhra on linguistic grounds intensified demands from other regions for statehood based on language, forcing the central government to set up a commission to examine the issue comprehensively.

masteryZone.q: How did the 1956 States Reorganisation Act change the administrative divisions of India?
masteryZone.sol: It abolished the four-fold classification (Part A, B, C, and D states) and the institution of Rajpramukh, replacing it with a simplified division consisting of 14 States and 6 Union Territories.

masteryZone.q: India and a neighboring state decide to resolve a border dispute by delineating a river boundary, resulting in a minor swap of patrol areas. Analyse if a constitutional amendment is required.
masteryZone.sol: No constitutional amendment is required. The Supreme Court in 1969 ruled that settlement of boundary disputes does not involve cession of territory and can be implemented by executive action alone.

masteryZone.q: Explain the evolution of linguistic states in India and the role of the reorganisation commissions.
masteryZone.sol: Post-independence, there were intense demands for reorganizing states linguistically. The Dhar Commission (1948) and JVP Committee (1948) rejected language to prioritize unity and administration. However, the death of Potti Sriramulu led to Andhra's creation in 1953, opening the floodgates. The Fazl Ali Commission (1953) accepted language as a factor but rejected the 'one language-one state' model. This led to the States Reorganisation Act of 1956, establishing 14 states and 6 UTs, laying the ground for India's linguistic federalism.
